key_insight: Adversarially suppressing specific clinical covariates can reveal whether a prostate MRI grading model relies on harmful shortcuts or useful disease-related signal.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help build MRI-based prostate cancer grading models that generalize better by separating irrelevant patient info from clinically informative predictors.
method: Model MRI appearance and ISUP grade as linked to latent tumor pathology.
Suppress one clinical covariate at a time with an adversarial objective while preserving grade prediction.
Compare performance changes to label each variable as nuisance, proxy, or task-relevant.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on 2,903 prostate MRI exams with external validation on 576 patients, and covariate suppression changed AUC in both helpful and harmful directions depending on the variable.
watch_item: A drop or gain in AUC after suppression suggests association, not definitive causality, so findings should be validated across sites and model settings.
paper_title: Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading
